subject: cardboardRobot
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
Style: cardboard craft.

spec.name: Cardboard Box Robot Kid
spec.description: A cheerful kid in a homemade corrugated-cardboard robot costume, standing in a T-pose with a face window in the box helmet, foil-wrapped tube sleeves, bottle-cap dials and duct-tape seams.
spec.layout: Kid about 1.2 m tall in the box, 1.46 m with the antennas. Front is +Z, left is +X. From the floor up: red sneakers (y 0 to 0.08); cardboard shin boxes over blue leggings (to 0.30); bare knees and thighs of leggings to the torso box bottom (y 0.52); the big torso box (y 0.52 to 1.02, 0.52 wide, 0.38 deep) with a control panel on the front; a smaller helmet box (y 1.02 to 1.36, 0.42 wide, 0.39 deep) sitting on top. The kid's face shows through a rectangular window cut in the front of the helmet. Arms stick out sideways through round holes in the torso box sides at y 0.92, in a T-pose with palms down, wearing foil-wrapped cardboard-tube sleeves with open fingers. Everything built by the costume is flat-shaded cardboard craft: kraft-brown box faces with a lighter inner-corrugation colour on every cut edge (a thin darker-brown layer strip along the cut rim of every hole and flap, showing the wavy corrugation as small ridge parts), tan masking-tape strips across all seams and corners, dark marker outlines and hand-drawn symbols, bottle-cap and button lights in bright colours, silver foil on tubes, and white hot-glue blobs at joins. Shapes are chunky, slightly imperfect boxes: flaps a few degrees off square, tape strips a bit crooked. The kid is a stylised chunky child with a big head, round cheeks and big eyes. Only the legs touch the floor.

parts.builds: The kid's own head and neck, seen through the helmet's face window. Chunky stylised child: a rounded-box skull about 0.19 wide, 0.23 tall and 0.2 deep centred on headCenter, a short neck cylinder from the torso down to the head (skin, with a little skinShade under the chin), and a separate lower jaw/chin piece on the jaw joint so the mouth can open. Face on the front (z about 0.13): two big readable eyes (eyeWhite ellipsoid, iris disc, dark pupil, tiny white highlight, small marker-brown upper lid line), thin brows in hair colour, a small button nose, round cheek blobs in cheek colour with a few freckle dots in skinShade, an upper lip and lower lip (lips colour) with a dark mouth gap and two small white front teeth in a happy open grin. Small ears at the sides (inside the helmet, partly hidden). Messy hair in hair colour: a solid cap on the skull plus 8 to 12 overlapping spiky tufts sticking up and out, a fringe over the brow, and a tuft at the back; the hair stays inside the helmet box (below y 1.35). Keep everything inside x +-0.1, below the helmet top, and nothing in front of z 0.15 so the face reads through the window.
parts.attaches: Neck rides neck and head joints and starts at neckBase (hidden in the torso top); skull is centred on headCenter and rides head; the lower jaw rides jaw at jawPivot. The helmet part surrounds it without touching.

parts.builds: The cardboard box helmet around the kid's head: five thin kraft slabs (left, right, back, top, front with a rectangular window about 0.24 wide x 0.22 tall centred on faceWindow, built as frame strips around the opening) forming a box x +-0.21, y 1.02 to 1.36, z -0.19 to 0.2, open at the bottom. Cut edges of the window show a lighter innerBoard rim with small corrugation ridge strips. Details: two tape strips across the top seam and one down the front corner; marker-drawn eyebrow-shaped angry/friendly slits above the window; hand-drawn marker grille mouth lines under the window; round ear dials on each side (a kraftDark disc with a foil bottle-cap, a marker tick mark ring and a pointer) at x +-0.21; two antennas on top (a thin foil-wrapped skewer rod with a coiled spring-like wire, topped with a lampRed and a lampYellow bottle-cap ball), the left one a little taller; a small egg-carton-style lampCyan cup light on the top front; a foil-wrapped disc 'speaker' on the top back; a paper label with marker scribble 'ROBO' lettering built from small marker bars on the helmet forehead strip; white hot-glue blobs at corners; bottom front edge flap folded slightly outward. Everything seated on the box faces.
parts.attaches: Sits on the torso's top rim at neckBase height y 1.02 and rides the head joint; window centred on faceWindow in front of kidHead; helmetTop mount is the top face for the antennas.

parts.builds: The big cardboard torso box x +-0.26, y 0.52 to 1.02, z -0.19 to 0.19, built from thick kraft slabs with visible corrugated cut edges (thin darker strips plus tiny ridge bars) around the open top and bottom, riding the chest and hips joints. Round arm holes at x +-0.26, y 0.92, radius 0.055, each with a rim of innerBoard and a ring of small corrugation ridges. Front control panel on torsoFrontPanel: a slightly raised kraftLight rectangular plate 0.34 wide x 0.3 tall, outlined with marker, holding a row of 3 bottle-cap lights (lampRed, lampYellow, lampGreen) with marker outline rings, two round dials (foil disc with marker tick marks and a pointer), a grid of 6 square paper-and-marker buttons, a lampCyan display strip with a marker zig-zag waveform, a hand-drawn marker heart and a small marker-red 'ON' lever with a crooked handle, and a sliding paper label. Side faces: marker-drawn gear symbol and rivet dots; back: a tape-attached foil 'battery pack' box with a coiled wire loop and two lamp bulbs. Tape strips across seams and each vertical corner, crooked; hot-glue blobs; cardboard shoulder flaps folded up and out of the top rim at x +-0.24 (not covering the helmet); two shirt-yellow strap loops over the shoulders visible at the top rim front and back; a bottom rim with a few folded flaps and a leggings-coloured shorts waist peeking just below the box between the legs. All details are separate parts in their own colours seated on the faces.
parts.attaches: Top rim at y 1.02 supports the helmetBox at neckBase; arm holes at shoulderL/shoulderR let the arms' sleeves exit; bottom rim at torsoBottom y 0.52 where the legs leave at hipL/hipR.

parts.builds: Both arms in an extended T-pose with palms down along x from the torso holes: from each shoulder a shirt-yellow sleeve stub pokes out of the arm hole (x 0.25 to 0.3), then a cardboard-tube upper-arm sleeve wrapped in foil (foil colour with foilShine highlight strips and foilDark crinkle ridge parts, 8-sided tube, radius about 0.05) to the elbow, an elbow gap of shirt-yellow showing at elbowL/elbowR, then a forearm foil tube (radius about 0.047) ending at the wrist with a kraft cardboard cuff ring (tube slice) plus tape band and a bottle-cap lamp (lampRed on the left cuff, lampGreen on the right) on the cuff top. Hands are kid skin: a chunky palm block and four fingers (index, middle, ring, pinky) each a two-segment capsule and a thumb angled forward/down, spread slightly and extended, with tiny knuckle dots and small nails in skinShade, on the finger and thumb joints. Add a few marker dashes and white glue blobs on the foil sleeves and a strip of tape spiralling on each upper arm. Left arm at +X, right arm at -X, mirrored.
parts.attaches: Roots at shoulderL/shoulderR just inside the torso arm holes and runs outward along x through elbowL/R and wristL/R to the fingertips; joints are the shoulder, elbow, wrist and digit joints of each side.

parts.builds: Both legs standing straight and slightly apart (feet at x +-0.08, toes forward), for floor contact. Blue leggings tubes (leggings colour, radius about 0.055 thigh tapering to 0.045 at the shin) from the hips at y 0.55 down through knees at y 0.3 to the ankles, with small knee patches in a slightly lighter blue. Over each shin a cardboard 'robot boot' box (kraft slabs, 0.14 wide x 0.22 tall x 0.15 deep, y 0.09 to 0.3) with a corrugated cut rim at top and bottom, a tape strip across the front, a marker-drawn bolt cross or arrow, and a small bottle-cap lamp (lampYellow on left, lampCyan on right) on the front, plus white glue blobs. Below, chunky red sneakers (sneaker colour) with white soles (sole colour, flat slab y 0 to 0.025), a rounded toe cap bump extending forward to about z 0.17, a tongue and lace pieces in paper colour, a heel tab, and small marker scuff marks. Mirror left (+X) and right (-X). Feet lowest points rest on y = 0.
parts.attaches: Thighs start inside the torso box at hipL/hipR (y 0.55) and leave its bottom at torsoBottom y 0.52; chains pass through kneeL/R and ankleL/R to toeL/R; the shin boxes are centred on the shin between knee and ankle.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the proportions for a cardboard-box robot costume on a kid: a boxy torso around 0.5m wide and 0.55m tall, arms out in a resting pose, and a helmet-style head box with a cutout window so the kid's face shows through.

Now I'm breaking the costume into parts - a head box with face window and antennas, a torso box with control panel details and arm holes, foil-wrapped arm sleeves with the kid's own hands/fingers peeking out as makeshift claws, and legs with cardboard shin covers and shoes.

I'm working through exact height and position values - hip joints around y=0.55, torso box spanning roughly 0.5 to 1.0 in height, with legs emerging below the box bottom down to the floor, figuring out proportions so the costume box sits naturally over a kid's actual leg length.

Now I'm placing shoulders at y=0.93 with arms extending outward in a T-pose, calculating hand positions and overall width when arms are extended, then moving up to position the neck and a helmet-style head box above it.

The helmet sits atop the torso box with the head and neck nested inside, antennas poking up near 1.45. Now I'm laying out the joint hierarchy starting from hips as root, through spine1, toward the chest.

Mapping arm joints next: shoulders at the sides, running through elbow and wrist down to compact kid-sized hands, keeping the whole arm span within roughly ±0.76 on the x-axis.

Now I'm defining finger joints — thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky per hand, each as a single digit joint parented to the wrist, giving ten total. Then I'm laying out the legs with hip, knee, ankle, and toe positions down each side, and starting on the jaw hinge point.

For the actual parts, I'm splitting the character into a kid's head (skull, face, eyes, ears, hair, neck, freckles) with its own budget, and a separate cardboard helmet box with a face window, flaps, antennas, ear dials, and lights.

Then I'm adding a torso box with panel buttons, dials, corrugated edges, arm holes, straps, belt, and pelvis; arms with sleeves and foil cuffs; and legs with cardboard shin boxes and shoes. Total budget comes to 960, so I need to trim it down to fit under 900 by reducing each part's allocation to roughly 150-200 points.

I'm also settling on the cardboard craft palette: kraft brown, lighter tan, dark edge brown, and corrugation line colors for that textured look.

Now I'm picking out the full color scheme - tan tape, black/red/blue markers, silver and dark foil, paper white, plus skin tones, hair, cheek blush, blue leggings, red sneakers with white soles, and glowing bottle-cap lights in yellow, red, green, and cyan for the robot costume's lit-up features.

I'm also working out the sleeve details - yellow shirt sleeves hidden under foil tubes with a foil-wrapped forearm, bare-skin hands with fingers visible, and a shirt cuff peeking through. Then I'm mapping out all the mount points for the figure's joints and anchors - neck base, head center, face window, helmet top/bottom, shoulders, torso bottom, hips, wrist, and ankle positions.

Now I'm sizing the helmet box and fitting the kid's head inside it, adjusting the skull radius and center position so the face sits properly behind a front window opening - making the head a bit bigger and more stylized so it reads well through the visor gap, with the window sized around 0.24 wide by 0.22 tall.

I'm also working out the torso box dimensions with arm holes on the sides and a neck opening at top where the helmet connects, figuring out how the ears tuck inside the helmet walls without poking through.

Now I'm sketching the leg structure: hip joints inside the torso box, thigh cylinders of a set radius, and cardboard-style rectangular shin boxes for the lower legs.

Going down to boots, feet occupy y 0–0.08 with toes extending toward z 0.15, and the overall figure stands about 1.52 wide by 1.46 tall by 0.42 deep, accounting for arms, helmet, antenna, and glowing eye knobs.

Now I'm planning the final write-up: layout text, a limited color palette, mount points, joint hierarchy, and detailed parts list, starting the parent chain from the hips as root up through the neck joint.

I'm placing the spine, chest, neck, head, and jaw joints with their positions and directions, working out where the jaw hinge should pivot relative to the head and chin, then moving down to the wrist, palm, and finger joint positions for the hands.

Still placing joints...

Now I'm budgeting the part costs — head, helmet, torso, arms, legs totaling around 860 — and working out the bounding box for the arms so the sleeve geometry clears the torso hole properly.
